subject: general
question: P and Q travel a distance of 120 km such that the speed of P is faster than Q. The sum of their speeds is 75 km/h and together they took the total time of 6 hours and 40 minutes. Then the speed of Q (in km/h) is
solution:
**Given:**

Distance travelled = 120 km

Sum of speeds of P and Q = 75 km/hr

Total time taken by both = 6 hours 40 min

**Concept used:**

Speed = distance /time

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a - b)² = a2 + b2 - 2ab

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of P be p km/hr and Q be q km/hr

q + p = 75 km/hr ----(i)

According to the question,

(120/p) + (120/q) = 6 hours and 40 minutes or 20/3 hours [As 1 hour = 60 minutes]

⇒ [(120q + 120p)/pq] = 20/3

⇒ 360q + 360p = 20pq ----(ii)

By multiplying eq (i) with 360 we get,

360q + 360p = 75 × 360

Now,

20pq = 75 × 360

⇒ pq = (75 × 360)/20

⇒ pq = 1350

Again,

(q + p)² = 5625

⇒ q² + p² + 2pq = 5625

⇒ q2 + p2 + 2pq - 4pq = 5625 - 4 × 1350

⇒ q2 + p2 - 2pq = 5625 - 5400

⇒ (q - p)² = 225

⇒ (q - p) = 15 ----(iii)

From eq (i) and eq (iii) we get

q = 30 and p = 45

So, speed of P is 45 km/h and Q is 30 km/h

**∴ The speed of Q (in km/h) is 30.**
